chunks.arabic_text: الكَافِي: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى، عَن مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ، عَن عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ، عَن عَنبَسَةَ بْنِ بِجَادٍ الْعَابِدِ، عَن جَابِرٍ، عَن أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Anbasa ibn Bijad al-Abdi, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كُنَّا عِنْدَهُ وَذَكَرُوا سُلْطَانَ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ فَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: لَا يَخْرُجُ عَلَى هِشَامٍ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا قَتَلَهُ، قَالَ: وَذَكَرَ مَلَكَهُ عِشْرِينَ سَنَةً، قَالَ: فَجَزِعْنَا، فَقَالَ: مَا لَكُمْ إِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ أَنْ يُهْلِكَ سُلْطَانَ قَوْمٍ أَمَرَ الْمَلَكَ فَأَسْرَعَ بِسَيْرِ الْفُلْكِ فَقَدَرَ عَلَى مَا يُرِيدُ؟ قَالَ: فَقُلْنَا لِزَيْدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ هَذِهِ الْمَقَالَةَ، فَقَالَ: إِنِّي شَهِدْتُ هِشَامًا وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ يُسْبُ عِنْدَهُ فَلَمْ يَنْكُرْ ذَلِكَ وَلَمْ يُغَيِّرْهُ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ لَمْ يَكُنْ إِلَّا أَنَا وَابْنِي لَخَرَجْتُ عَلَيْهِ!

translations.en: We were with him when the rulers of Bani Umayya were mentioned, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'No one will rise against Hisham except that he will kill him.' He said: 'He mentioned his rule lasted twenty years.' He said: 'We were overcome with grief,' so he said: 'What is wrong with you? Don't you know that if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wishes to destroy the ruler of a people, He commands the angel, who hastens swiftly through the celestial sphere, and accomplishes what he intends?' He said: 'We relayed these words to Zayd (peace be upon him), and he said: I witnessed Hisham while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was being abused in his presence, yet he did not repudiate it nor did he change it. So by Allah, if there were no one except myself and my son, I would still rise against him!'

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the theological justification for Zayd ibn Ali's uprising against the Umayyad Caliph Hisham, framing it not merely as political dissent but as a response to divine decree and prophetic precedent. The Imam explains that Hisham's twenty-year reign was ordained by God, yet his failure to correct the public desecration of the Prophet Muhammad served as a critical sign of illegitimacy. Consequently, Zayd ibn Ali asserts that even if only he and his son were involved, the Prophet's silence regarding the abuse of his honor necessitated armed resistance to restore religious integrity.
en.seo_question: Why did Zayd ibn Ali decide to rebel against the Umayyads despite the Prophet's presence?
